subject: Pilot: Short runway — bridge fee vs 3-week extension (VoxHealth)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@voxhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask — pilot running out of runway

Rafael,

Thanks again for the support so far. We just ran the latest integration tests and the pilot burn has been faster than expected; unless we extend the pilot we risk not having enough signal for the final evaluation next sprint. Our internal deadline for decisioning is 8/10.

Two options we can live with: a) a 3-week extension on the existing timeboxed pilot with no change to the invoice schedule, or b) a short bridge (one-week) plus a small bridging fee to cover extra capacity while we finish our evaluation. Procurement would prefer the extension (less paperwork). From our side, engineering can remain available for an extra week or two but procurement needs a written amendment.

Can you outline what Redwood would consider reasonable? We want to avoid escalating for credits if possible.

Thanks,
Daniel
VP Product, VoxHealth

--
Attachment: VoxHealth_Metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@voxhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pilot running out of runway

Daniel — appreciate the heads up. Short answer: we can do either but need to align on billing and capacity. Two practical proposals from our side: 

Option A (time extension): 3-week extension on the same pilot SOW; no additional per-token charge, same tooling and observability. We'll add a one-page addendum (no price change) and keep engineering support at the current SLA. Procurement-friendly but requires a signed amendment.

Option B (bridge + fee): 7-day bridge window today + a $2,500 bridging fee to reserve burst capacity and priority routing; this avoids an immediate contract amendment and lets you finish evaluation sooner. If you convert to a committed plan within 30 days we will credit the $2,500 against the first month.

Marissa — any operational caveats on engineering/priority routing for Option B? Ben, looping you for approval on the credit-forward clause.

I can put the addendum in DocuSign today if you pick A, or sign off on the bridge fee and we’ll provision surge capacity immediately.

Best,
Rafael
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: POC_Addendum_Draft.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-27T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pilot running out of runway

Thanks Rafa / Daniel. Operational notes: 

- Option A (3-week extension): low friction. We keep the same GPU pool allocation and KV cache settings. No change to telemetry. We recommend a short success milestone (two checkpoints) so we can scope live support hours — otherwise risk of unmetered ENG time.

- Option B (bridge + fee): we can provision priority routing within 24 hours, but it will consume burst units from the pool. The $2.5k credit-if-convert makes sense to sales but needs Ben's sign-off. Also recommend we include a clause limiting total reserved tokens per day during the bridge to avoid surprise overage.

Suggested hybrid: grant a 10-calendar-day extension (shorter than 3w) + 8 hours of named Redwoods engineering office hours + a small non-refundable $1,000 admin fee to cover priority allocation. That splits the difference, makes procurement slightly happier (smaller amendment), and reduces paperwork for both sides.

If Daniel agrees, I'll draft the addendum with the milestone language + token cap and push to DocuSign.

Marissa
Senior CS Manager, Redwood Inference
